title: Formal Jacobian minors detect a nondegenerate binary quadratic hypersurface
statement: Let $F$ be a field, $n\ge2$, $T=F[[t_1,\ldots,t_n]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], $\mathfrak n=(t_1,\ldots,t_n)$, and $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_s)\subseteq\mathfrak n$. Set $R=T/I$ with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak n/I$. Let $J\subseteq R$ be the ideal generated by the images of the $(n-1)\times(n-1)$ minors [def-weil-matrix, def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant] of the matrix $(\partial f_j/\partial t_i)$, where formal differentiation is termwise differentiation of power series. Then the following are equivalent: (a) $\operatorname{depth}(R)=1$ [def-weil-pbc-depth] and $J=\mathfrak m$; (b) $R$ is isomorphic as a complete local $F$-algebra to $F[[u,v]]/(au^2+buv+cv^2)$ for some $a,b,c\in F$ with $b^2-4ac\ne0$. (c) $R$ is isomorphic as a ring (not necessarily $F$-linearly) to $F[[u,v]]/(au^2+buv+cv^2)$ for some $a,b,c\in F$ with $b^2-4ac\ne0$. The discriminant condition means that the linear map with matrix $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}2a&b\\ b&2c\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ is invertible, including in characteristic $2$.

source.place: Tags 0C4C (lemma-fitting-ideal), equivalence (1) and (3), and 0C49 (lemma-nodal-algebraic), conditions (1) and (3); condition (1) of 0C49 (reduced, embedding dimension 2, a nondegenerate quadric in Sym^2 of the cotangent space vanishing in m^2/m^3) is invariant under ring isomorphisms, the residue-field isomorphism transporting the quadric, which gives (c) to (b). n>=2 avoids the negative-minor convention.

proof.text: First put the presentation into minimal coordinates, without any assumption (a), (b) or (c). By [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-field-cohen-regular-complete], $T$ is complete Noetherian regular local of dimension $n$. Let $t$ be the dimension of $(I+\mathfrak n^2)/\mathfrak n^2$. Choose $g_1,\ldots,g_t\in I$ whose linear terms are a basis of this space, and extend their linear terms by those of $z_1,\ldots,z_e\in\mathfrak n$ to a basis of $\mathfrak n/\mathfrak n^2$, where $e=n-t$. This space has basis the original variables by coefficient comparison. By [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators], this list generates $\mathfrak n$, so it is a regular system of $n$ parameters. By [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-full-coordinates-field] it is a system of $F$-algebra power-series coordinates. Replace each original generator $f_j$ by $h_j=f_j(0,\ldots,0,z_1,\ldots,z_e)$; their differences belong to $(g_1,\ldots,g_t)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-quotient-variables]. Consequently $I=(g_1,\ldots,g_t,h_1,\ldots,h_s)$ and $R\cong S/H$, where $S=F[[z_1,\ldots,z_e]]$, $\mathfrak p=(z_1,\ldots,z_e)$ and $H=(h_1,\ldots,h_s)\subseteq\mathfrak p^2$. The last inclusion follows because every linear term of an element of $I$ lies in the span of the $g_i$. Thus $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$ has $F$-basis the classes of the $z_i$ and dimension $e$.

source.place: 0C4C (lemma-fitting-ideal), unit-derivative elimination; simultaneous version using a basis of linear terms.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-formal-jacobian-minor-invariance], compute $J$ with the coordinates and generators from step 1. The Jacobian is block diagonal with an identity block of size $t$ and the residual matrix $B=(\partial h_j/\partial z_i)$; the off-diagonal blocks are zero because the $h_j$ involve only the $z_i$. If $e=0$ or $e=1$, the identity block supplies an $(n-1)$-minor equal to $1$, so $J=R$. If $e\ge2$, its $(n-1)$-minors are either zero or signed minors of $B$ of size at least $e-1$. Every $(e-1)$-minor occurs by adjoining the whole identity block; larger minor ideals are contained in it by [lem-trf-fitting-ideal-minor-inclusions](1). Hence $J$ is exactly the ideal of $(e-1)$-minors of $B$. Since $H\subseteq\mathfrak p^2$, the entries of $B$ are in $\mathfrak m$, and therefore $J\subseteq\mathfrak m^{e-1}$.

source.place: 0C4C, block-matrix calculation after elimination; all minor sizes, including e=0 and e=1.

proof.text: Assume (a). The equality $J=\mathfrak m$ rules out $e=0,1$ by step 2, since the maximal ideal is proper. If $e\ge3$, step 2 gives $\mathfrak m\subseteq\mathfrak m^2$, hence $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak m^2$. The maximal ideal is generated by the $e$ variables, so [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators], applied to this finite $R$-module, gives $\mathfrak m=0$. Then $R$ is a field and has depth $0$: every element of its maximal ideal is zero, and zero is not a nonzerodivisor on the nonzero module $R$. This contradicts (a). Thus $e=2$.

source.place: 0C4C, minor-order bound and Nakayama argument forcing two remaining variables.

proof.text: Write $S=F[[u,v]]$ and $\mathfrak p=(u,v)$ in the presentation of step 1. By [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-field-cohen-regular-complete], $S$ is regular local of dimension $2$. Its quotient $S/H\cong R$ has depth $1$, and $H\subseteq\mathfrak p^2\subseteq\mathfrak p$. Apply [lem-trf-regular-surface-depth-one-principal] to obtain $H=(f)$ with $f\ne0$. Since $f\in H$, it has no constant or linear term. By [lem-trf-formal-jacobian-minor-invariance] replace the residual generators by $f$; the original $J$, as computed in step 2, is now $(\overline{f_u},\overline{f_v})$.

source.place: 0C4C, application of 0C48(2) to the two-variable quotient and change to its principal generator.

proof.text: Let $Q=au^2+buv+cv^2$ be the degree-two part of $f$. Termwise differentiation gives $f_u\equiv2au+bv$ and $f_v\equiv bu+2cv$ modulo $\mathfrak p^2$. Because $H\subseteq\mathfrak p^2$, the classes of $u,v$ form a basis of $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$. The equality $J=\mathfrak m$ therefore says that the two displayed linear forms span a two-dimensional space. Their matrix has determinant $4ac-b^2$, which is consequently nonzero. This proves the required discriminant condition in every characteristic.

source.place: 0C4C, final quadratic-term computation; discussion before 0C49 defining nondegeneracy.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-formal-binary-morse] to the series $f$ of step 4, whose quadratic part is nondegenerate by step 5. Its continuous $F$-algebra automorphism sends $(f)$ to $(Q)$, so it induces a complete local $F$-algebra isomorphism $R\cong F[[u,v]]/(Q)$. All algebraic isomorphisms here preserve the maximal ideals and their powers, hence the adic topologies. This proves (a) implies (b).

source.place: 0C49, successive removal of higher-order terms in (2) implies (3).

proof.text: Forgetting $F$-linearity and continuity in (b) gives the ring isomorphism required by (c).

To prove (c) implies (a), first compute the depth of the model $M=F[[u,v]]/(Q)$ in (c). Put $S_0=F[[u,v]]$. By [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-field-cohen-regular-complete], $S_0$ is a Noetherian local domain of dimension $2$. The regular-parameter theorem [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence] makes $u,v$ a regular sequence, so its depth is at least $2$. It is at most $2$ by [lem-weil-pbc-depth-le-support-dimension], since the support of $S_0$ as its own module is its entire prime spectrum, of dimension $2$. Thus its depth is exactly $2$. Nondegeneracy implies $Q\ne0$, so multiplication by $Q$ is injective on the domain $S_0$, and $Q\in(u,v)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-depth-drops-by-one], $S_0/(Q)$ has module depth $1$ over $S_0$; [lem-weil-pbc-depth-over-quotient-ring] identifies this with its ring depth. A ring isomorphism preserves maximal ideals and regular sequences, so (c) gives $\operatorname{depth}R=1$.

source.place: 0C4C, explicit depth computation for the quadratic model; standard depth ingredients in Algebra as used in 0C49.

proof.text: The ring isomorphism of (c) induces an isomorphism of residue fields $\sigma:F\to F$ and a $\sigma$-semilinear bijection on cotangent spaces (multiplication by a residue class is defined using any lift, so it commutes with the induced maps). The model has cotangent dimension $2$, since $(Q)\subseteq(u,v)^2$. Thus $e=2$ in step 1. As in step 4, [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-field-cohen-regular-complete] and [lem-trf-regular-surface-depth-one-principal], using the depth just proved, give $H=(f)$ for $f\ne0$ with $f\in\mathfrak p^2$. No coefficient-field compatibility of the given ring isomorphism has been asserted.

source.place: 0C49, invariance of the intrinsic cotangent-space condition under a ring isomorphism, followed by 0C48(2).

proof.text: Use the degree-two multiplication map: a homogeneous binary quadratic in the classes of a cotangent basis maps to its product class in $\mathfrak m^2/\mathfrak m^3$. For the model its kernel is the one-dimensional span of $Q$: modulo $(u,v)^3$, a multiple of $Q$ is just its constant multiplier times $Q$. This kernel and its generator transfer through the ring isomorphism of (c). Under a change of cotangent basis by $P\in\mathrm{GL}_2(F)$, and the residue-field isomorphism $\sigma$, the polar matrix becomes $P^{\mathsf T}\sigma(B)P$, so its determinant becomes $(\det P)^2\sigma(\det B)\ne0$. In the minimal presentation $S/(f)$ of step 9, the degree-two kernel is zero if $f$ has order at least $3$, and otherwise is the span of the degree-two part $f_2$: again compare constant terms of multipliers of $f$ modulo $\mathfrak p^3$. Hence $f_2$ is a nonzero scalar multiple of a nondegenerate quadratic. Its two partial derivatives form a basis modulo $\mathfrak m^2$, by the explicit matrix calculation in step 5. By [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators] they generate $\mathfrak m$. Finally [lem-trf-formal-jacobian-minor-invariance] and the block computation of step 2 identify their generated ideal with the original $J$. Thus $J=\mathfrak m$; together with step 8 this is (a), completing the three-way equivalence.

source.place: 0C49(1), intrinsic quadratic relation and its semilinear invariance; 0C4C, two-variable gradient computation.

proof_origin.place: Tags 0C4C (lemma-fitting-ideal), 0C48(2), 0C49; ring-isomorphism clause made explicit through the degree-two cotangent relation.

lean.statement: theorem formal_jacobian_quadratic_criterion (F : Type u) [Field F] (n s : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) (I : Ideal (MvPowerSeries (Fin n) F)) (hI : I ≤ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (MvPowerSeries (Fin n) F)) (f : Fin s → MvPowerSeries (Fin n) F) (hgen : I = Ideal.span (Set.range f)) : ((Ideal.depth (formalJacobianMaximalIdeal F n I) (MvPowerSeries (Fin n) F ⧸ I) = (1 : ℕ∞) ∧ formalJacobianIdeal F n s I f = formalJacobianMaximalIdeal F n I) ↔ ∃ (a b c : F), b ^ 2 - 4 * a * c ≠ 0 ∧ Nonempty ((MvPowerSeries (Fin n) F ⧸ I) ≃ₐ[F] (MvPowerSeries (Fin 2) F ⧸ Ideal.span ({MvPowerSeries.C a * (MvPowerSeries.X 0) ^ 2 + MvPowerSeries.C b * (MvPowerSeries.X 0 * MvPowerSeries.X 1) + MvPowerSeries.C c * (MvPowerSeries.X 1) ^ 2} : Set (MvPowerSeries (Fin 2) F))))) ∧ ((∃ (a b c : F), b ^ 2 - 4 * a * c ≠ 0 ∧ Nonempty ((MvPowerSeries (Fin n) F ⧸ I) ≃ₐ[F] (MvPowerSeries (Fin 2) F ⧸ Ideal.span ({MvPowerSeries.C a * (MvPowerSeries.X 0) ^ 2 + MvPowerSeries.C b * (MvPowerSeries.X 0 * MvPowerSeries.X 1) + MvPowerSeries.C c * (MvPowerSeries.X 1) ^ 2} : Set (MvPowerSeries (Fin 2) F))))) ↔ ∃ (a b c : F), b ^ 2 - 4 * a * c ≠ 0 ∧ Nonempty ((MvPowerSeries (Fin n) F ⧸ I) ≃+* (MvPowerSeries (Fin 2) F ⧸ Ideal.span ({MvPowerSeries.C a * (MvPowerSeries.X 0) ^ 2 + MvPowerSeries.C b * (MvPowerSeries.X 0 * MvPowerSeries.X 1) + MvPowerSeries.C c * (MvPowerSeries.X 1) ^ 2} : Set (MvPowerSeries (Fin 2) F)))))
